punchline: Sumo wrestlers one win short of a winning record won far more often than they should, and then lost more often the next time they met that opponent.
thirty_sec: In sumo, an eighth win lifts a wrestler about eleven places, far more than any other win. Two economists checked more than 32,000 top-division bouts. Wrestlers with seven wins on the last days won 12 to 16 points more often than expected, then lost more often when they met the same opponent again. They also found the extra wins vanished when media scrutiny was high. It reads like favors being traded, though the evidence is statistical, not proof of any single bout.
